$meta.replaces: v1 'Aurora, voice-first' (2026-08-17 .. 2026-08-19). Full replacement of colour, type, spacing, shape and layout, decided in docs/reports/owner-decision-2026-08-21-redesign-the-visual-language.md. The 52 published element ids are UNCHANGED — see components.md § Testid catalogue.
$meta.rule: Every value an implementer uses comes from this file. Reviewer C4 fails hardcoded design values.
$meta.contrast: Every text pair below computed by the WCAG 2.1 relative-luminance formula and listed in DESIGN.md ## Contrast. Minimum 4.5:1 normal text, 3:1 for rules and control boundaries that carry meaning.
$meta.accents: THE ACCENT SET IS CLOSED AT THREE, down from five. Meanings live in DESIGN.md ## Colour rules and are not restated here (L-004). green/success and the cyan|violet voice pair are RETIRED — DESIGN.md ## Colour rules 5 records what replaced each and why. Adding a fourth accent is a system decision that arrives with its own meaning.
$meta.specimen: docs/design/_shared/specimen.html — the rendered proof of this file. Every token below appears there in use.
$meta.revised: 2026-08-22 (T-220) — PANELS ON A CANVAS. The three long structural borders between layout regions — topbar bottom, col-panel left, composer top — are replaced by a panel pattern: the page is bg.sunken, each content region is a bg.base panel rounded at radius.md with a space.1 gap between. The 1px-rule third case (a container holding a different kind of thing) is rewritten: that boundary is now carried by elevation and ground, not by a line. AI reply bubble marks changed from border-left with squared corners to an inset pseudo clipped by overflow:hidden, so marked and unmarked replies have the same silhouette. Colour, type and spacing are UNCHANGED. Previous: T-210 softening (radius, border density, ultra answer).

family.ui: Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Helvetica Neue', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, system-ui, sans-serif
family.numeric: ui-monospace, 'SF Mono', 'JetBrains Mono', 'Roboto Mono', Menlo, Consolas, monospace

font.family_note: ONE UI family, plus one utility face for numerals. The anchor locks a single grotesque for display and body. Product copy is English (ADR-008), but a TASK TITLE IS USER CONTENT in whatever script the user types — the live store carries Vietnamese titles today — so the face that sets titles must hold at body size across heavy diacritics, which is where a display face chosen for English headings breaks first. Hierarchy is carried by size, weight, case and tracking — the Swiss method — not by a second voice. The numeric face is legal ONLY on times, dates, counts, durations and ids. Justification recorded in DESIGN.md ## Type.
font.size_note: ONE scale, three floors. The ramp and its ratio are shared; iOS lifts body to 17 (its own text baseline, and what Dynamic Type scales from) and Android sets meta to 14 (M3 bodyMedium). Nothing else diverges — platform paint never wins over the design system.
font.note: Body line-height 1.5 minimum, and body never below 16 on any platform. Both floors are set for arbitrary user-typed script, not for English: below 16 iOS zooms the page on focus and stacked tone marks lose their separation from the letter. label 11 is uppercase, tracked, and is for section eyebrows and NEW/EDITED markers only.

space_note: 4-based. gutter_mobile = 4, gutter_web = 5, section = 7. No value outside this scale appears in a mockup.

assign.none: GEOMETRY, NOT OBJECTS — a rule, the time-rail spine, a hairline, a full-bleed divider, a table cell edge. A line has no corners to soften.
assign.xs: the smallest painted objects, where 8 would read as a lozenge — tag, the NEW / EDITED marker, the priority chip, a colour swatch.
assign.sm_note_checkbox: The checkbox moved from xs to sm (8px on a 20px box — 40%) per owner decision: xs (4px) barely reads as rounded and looks square rather than pressable. At sm the checkbox is a clear squircle. One shape on all three platforms; the iOS circle (Apple Reminders convention) is dropped. Things 3, the closest comparable in DESIGN.md, uses a rounded square on iOS.
assign.sm: CONTROLS — button, field, textarea, segmented control, menu item, the Lists-rail nav row, the state chip, checkbox (moved from xs — 4px on 20px looked square, 8px reads as a pressable squircle).
assign.md: GROUNDS — the task row's hover / selected ground, card, banner, diff block, message bubble, skeleton, toast.
assign.lg: LAYERS THAT FLOAT — menu, dialog, popover, the web slide-over sheet. Pairs with shadow.overlay and never appears without it.
assign.xl: THE TOP TWO CORNERS of an iOS or Android bottom sheet, and nothing else. The bottom two are 0 — the sheet meets the screen edge.

radius.nesting_rule: CHECKABLE: an inner radius is never larger than its parent's, and where a child sits inset inside a parent, inner = parent minus the inset. A control at sm 8 inset by 4 inside a card at md 12 is correct; the same control at md inside it is the concentric-corner mistake, visible as a gap that thickens at each corner.
radius.note: v2's first pass set every structural component to 0 and argued it at length as the biggest shape change from v1. THE OWNER LOOKED AT THE RENDER AND IT READS HARD (owner-decision-2026-08-22). Radius is back, as a four-step scale that answers ONE question: what kind of thing is this? A line takes none; a small painted object takes xs; a control takes sm; a ground takes md; a floating layer takes lg. The scale stops at 16 for everyday surfaces on purpose — 24 and above is the wellness-app neighbourhood DESIGN.md ## Identity rejected by name, and softening the corners is not permission to move there. The bubble token from the first pass is RETIRED: a message bubble is a ground and takes md.

border.primary_tool: SPACE AND GROUND ARE THE PRIMARY STRUCTURING TOOLS. TYPE WEIGHT IS THE THIRD. THE 1PX RULE IS A SPECIALIST TOOL, NOT THE DEFAULT. This replaces v2's first-pass rule, which read `structure is a 1px rule, never a shadow` — and that rule was not merely applied too densely, it named the wrong primary tool. WHERE IT CAME FROM: Swiss and editorial grid systems, where the rule IS primary because PAPER HAS NO OTHER PLANES — no elevated ground, no hover, no cheap whitespace. A screen has all three, so the primary tool moved and this system did not move with it. A full box around every element reads as roughly 2013-2017. Current practice separates by space and by ground and reaches for a hairline sparingly.
border.when_a_line_earns_it: TWO CASES, each with a reason rather than a taste. (1) AN INPUT FIELD — the user must be able to see where to type. A field needs a boundary OR a distinct ground, and it needs one of the two; WCAG 1.4.11 is about exactly this. (2) A DENSE, TABLE-LIKE ROW where the eye scans across several values — a type ramp, a contrast table, a settings table. There the rule is the measure, not decoration. THE FORMER CASE 3 (a container holding a different kind of thing) IS REWRITTEN AS A PANEL RULE: that boundary — the conversation beside the task list, the rail beside both — is now carried by the layout.panel pattern: each region is a bg.base ground on a bg.sunken canvas, rounded at radius.md, separated by layout.panel.gap. The elevation and ground do the work the line used to do, with zero added lines. OUTSIDE THESE TWO, USE SPACE OR GROUND. THE TASK ROW IS `time - checkbox - title`, WHICH IS NOT A TABLE: space separates those perfectly well, and it is what Things 3 and Apple Reminders — the two closest comparables to this product — do between task rows, which is nothing.
border.separation_order: When you have decided a boundary is needed: GROUND FIRST (bg.sunken behind a group, bg.raised in front of one), THEN SPACE (space.5 around it), THEN a line, and only if neither of the first two reads.
border.density_rule: A SYMPTOM CHECK, NOT THE RULE — the rule is primary_tool and when_a_line_earns_it above. This number is what catches the drift back. CHECKABLE, AND IT COUNTS PAINTED LINES, NOT `border` DECLARATIONS. A painted line is any 1-2px line an element puts on screen: a border-* edge, a ::before / ::after bar, or a 1px-tall div. Counting declarations is defeated by moving a line into a div, and THIS SYSTEM ALREADY DID THAT — app-shell.html draws its five row separators as `.row-rule` divs and its list spine as `.list::before`, so a border grep misses six of the thirteen lines on screen. Both budgets below are PER RENDERED STATE PER BREAKPOINT, measured inside the app frame; a design-tool state switcher is not the app.
border.budget_note: STRUCTURAL LINES <= 8. A structural line separates content from content: a pane boundary, a section rule, a row separator, the time-rail spine. MEASURED on app-shell.html at ultra, state tasks-default, before this revision: 13 — 7 border edges plus the list spine plus 5 row-rule divs. AFTER the same file is rebuilt to when_a_line_earns_it the count is 4, well inside the budget, which is the point: the budget is not the target, the three earned cases are, and a file that satisfies them lands far below 8 on its own. FULL BOXES <= 5, every one on box_allowlist. MEASURED in the same state before this revision: 9, of which the message bubble and the primary button are not on the list. The budget is per state because the state nobody opens is where the count creeps back.
border.box_allowlist: A full box is legal on exactly two kinds of thing. (1) A CONTROL WHOSE OUTLINE IS THE CONTROL, sitting on the same ground as its surroundings: checkbox, radio, field, textarea, the quiet/secondary/danger-quiet button variants, the idle mic. (2) A LAYER FLOATING OVER ANOTHER: menu, dialog, popover, toast, the web sheet — and there the box pairs with shadow.overlay. NOTHING ELSE. A message bubble, a diff block, a banner, a card and a task row are GROUNDS, not boxes: they separate by bg.sunken or bg.raised at radius.md. A filled button is a ground too and carries no border.
border.note: hairline is decorative separation (color.bg.hairline); rule is a boundary that carries meaning and uses color.bg.rule, which clears 3:1. mark 2 is the accent left-rule on an assistant message that changed something — a left mark is ONE line and is not a box, so it survives the cut and counts as one structural line.

shadow.note: ONE shadow, and it is legal only on a layer that floats over another — sheet, menu, dialog, toast. Rows, cards, buttons and inputs carry no shadow at any state. A shadow used for emphasis instead of separation is a review failure.

control.note: minTarget is a hit-area floor met with hitSlop / padding, never by painting a bigger control. Row height is lg (52) on every platform, which already clears all three floors.

field.rule: A field has NO intrinsic width. It is width:100% of its form row, always. The HTML size attribute and any fixed px width on an input are forbidden. CHECKABLE: inside a form row wider than 320, any field rendering below min_rendered_width is a failure. This rule exists because the shipped task detail rendered 197px input stubs that clipped the task's own title — the class was used in JSX and styled nowhere, so the input fell back to the HTML default size=20.

panel.note: PANELS ON A CANVAS. Content regions float as bg.base panels on a bg.sunken canvas (the app background). Gap is space.1 (4px) between adjacent panels. Radius is radius.md (12px) — panels are GROUNDS, not floating layers, so they take md and not lg. The canvas is visible only at split and above; below split the single panel fills the viewport flush with no gap and no rounding. The panel pattern replaces the three long structural borders between layout regions (topbar bottom, col-panel left, composer top) and does the work with zero added lines. At wide all three columns — rail, Tasks, Talk — are separate panels. LINEAR, NOTION, VERCEL and current macOS sidebars all read this way.

layout.wide_rule: ABOVE desktop THE APP ADDS A COLUMN, NEVER A GUTTER. THREE frame tiers, and a fourth was drawn, rendered, compared and REJECTED — see two_column_tested_and_rejected. TIER 1, below split: one surface on screen, the frame is the pane. TIER 2, split up to wide: Tasks pane takes the frame minus the Talk panel. TIER 3, wide up to ultra: a permanent Lists rail (measure.rail) joins on the left and the Tasks pane takes what is left. At ultra the frame does NOT gain a fourth column: see ultra_answer. In every tier each frame column then applies content_column_rule, so a column wider than its measure centres its content instead of anchoring it left. Past frame_max the whole frame centres.
layout.ultra_answer: AT ULTRA THE FRAME IS TIER 3 AND THE ANSWER IS THAT NOTHING IS DRAWN ACROSS THE LEFTOVER. The owner called 1920 unusable after the previous pass had already made the leftover symmetric (220/220, down from 0/780), so the leftover was never the defect. MEASURED at 1920: the content column is 820 wide and a row's ink — time, checkbox, title — ends 409px in, so half of every row is empty. WHAT MADE THAT UGLY WAS THE LINE DRAWN ACROSS IT: five row separators running the full 820 turned half-empty rows into stretched hairlines on a very wide screen. Delete the separators and the same emptiness reads as margin. RENDERED PROOF: output/design-shots/appshell-1920.png (before) against exp-A-softonly-1920.png (row rules and pane borders removed, corners softened, nothing else changed).
layout.two_column_tested_and_rejected: A FOURTH TIER SPLITTING THE TASKS PANE INTO TWO TASK COLUMNS — the open list, and its next seven days — WAS SPECIFIED, BUILT AND RENDERED AT 1920 BEFORE BEING REJECTED. Evidence: output/design-shots/exp-C2-fair-1920.png, two columns at the full specified 590 each. THREE MEASURED REASONS IT LOST. (1) IT DOES NOT FIX THE EMPTY ROW. A row is half empty because a task is a short string; splitting the pane produces TWO columns of half-empty rows instead of one, and the left column's title still stops about 330px short of its own column edge. (2) IT DUPLICATES THE DIFFERENTIATOR. Two time rails means two spine rules on one screen, and the novelty budget was spent once, on one rail. (3) AT A NARROWER COLUMN THE TITLE WRAPS — the first, cruder run at about 430 per column wrapped two of five titles onto a second line, and the title is the one thing a todo list is made of. THE BORDER CHANGE CARRIED THE STATE AND THE LAYOUT CHANGE DID NOT. Recorded here so the next dispatch does not re-propose it: it is not untried, it is tried. RESIDUE, HONESTLY: at 1920 the lower half of the screen and the Talk panel are still largely empty. That is a SCREENS question about what those surfaces show, not a frame-tier question, and inventing a third structural answer without rendering it would repeat the mistake this entry records.
layout.content_column_rule: ONE CENTRING, AND IT IS AT THE CONTENT COLUMN. Each frame column (Lists rail, Tasks pane, Talk panel) holds exactly ONE content column, width min(pane minus two gutters, its measure token), CENTRED in its pane. Everything inside a content column is left-aligned and nothing inside it centres again. Leftover width is therefore always symmetric and always at the same level.
layout.fill_rule: CHECKABLE, and it is the underflow test design-check has never had. For every frame column, measure the leftover on each side of its content column; if the two differ by more than eight pixels, FAIL. v1's .tasks-col was max-width 720 with no margin auto, so at ultra it left zero on one side and 780 on the other — that asymmetry is the defect, and it is what this check names. A capped measure with symmetric leftover is not a defect and must not be reported as one.
layout.coverage_rule: CHECKABLE, second half. A frame column's content must cover at least fill_min_ratio of the column's inner width UNLESS the shortfall is explained by a declared measure token (measure.list_max, measure.form_max, measure.text_ch). A shortfall with no measure token behind it is a column that stopped growing for no stated reason.
layout.gap_rule: CHECKABLE: two text spans in the same row are never adjacent. Minimum gap between any two of them is space.2. v1's priority mark computed margin-left 0 and the glyphs touched the last letter of the task title.

breakpoints.note: Every width in this block is MEASURED by design-check. split and wide are the two widths at which layout BRANCHES; the rest are measurement stops. ultra was very nearly made a third branch point in the softening revision and was not — layout.two_column_tested_and_rejected records what was rendered and why it lost. The previous system declared four and stopped at desktop, which is why its worst defect was invisible to every check and present in its own mockup. mobile and phone are both here because the floor and the real device differ. KEEP THIS NOTE FREE OF DIGITS, INCLUDING VERSION NUMBERS: design-check strips non-digits from every value in this block, so writing the previous system as a v-plus-digit yields a phantom breakpoint measured at one pixel. That is not hypothetical; it happened while this file was being written. WHY wide SITS WHERE IT DOES: it is the narrowest frame at which the Lists rail can arrive without the Tasks list getting narrower than it was one breakpoint earlier — rail plus list_max plus two gutters plus panel_max. Put the rail in at laptop instead and a user who maximises their window watches the list shrink, which is a regression dressed as a feature.

motion.rule: animate transform and opacity only. NO spring, NO bounce, NO breathing loop — v1 had a 2400ms aurora loop and a spring curve; both are retired with the gradient. The one continuous animation left is the listening rule, which grows linearly along the composer while the microphone is live and is the only thing on screen that moves without the user acting.
motion.reducedMotion: every animation collapses to an 80ms opacity change; end states (strikethrough, marks, the listening rule at full width) are fully kept.

mapping.note: Which state change uses which duration. Every entry names the change, the duration, the property, and what reduced-motion sees.

task_complete.what: row fades and slides right, strikethrough draws; reduced: instant, strikethrough kept

task_arrive.what: new row fades in from above; reduced: instant appear

task_delete.what: row fades and slides right; reduced: instant remove

reply_arrive.what: bubble fades up from below; reduced: instant appear

undo_bar_appear.what: slides up from the bottom; reduced: instant appear

list_reorder.what: rows animate to new positions; reduced: instant move

sheet_open.what: sheet slides up with scrim fade; reduced: instant, scrim kept

sheet_close.what: sheet slides down, scrim fades; reduced: instant

picker_open.what: picker expands from top; reduced: instant appear

listening_rule.what: accent rule grows linearly along composer; reduced: full width immediately, but kept — it is information

listColor.note: A fixed palette of swatches for user lists. Default is grey (index 0). The colour appears as a dot in list rows (rail, menu) and travels into the task row so a task shows its list without a text label. ALWAYS REDUNDANT — the list name is always present beside the dot. Seven swatches is the maximum that fits on one row in a 288px drawer without wrapping. System collections (Today, Upcoming, Done, Inbox) carry icons, not dots — icon means system, dot means yours.
listColor.row_rule: A list's colour is carried by its dot; the row's ground means selection. A coloured row background would put two meanings in one channel and force per-colour text contrast.

icon.note: stroke 1.5 and square caps, down from v1's 1.8 round — the icons sit against 1px rules and a rounder heavier stroke reads as a different system. No emoji as UI icons; no unicode glyph standing in for an icon.

haptic.note: TARGET, not current behaviour — carried unchanged from v1 with its warning intact: no expo-haptics is in the build, so nothing below fires today. It binds whoever adds the first mobile animation, in the same change.
